result.summary: Fixes a Windows-specific bug where the bitcoin.exe wrapper used _execvp and exited immediately after spawning its child, so callers (scripts, test frameworks) could never observe the child's real exit code or captured output. The fix switches to _spawnvp(_P_NOWAIT)+_cwait and forwards the child's status, adds an msvcrt-specific EINVAL-to-ENOENT workaround for path lookup, and fixes an errno category bug that produced a misleading Win32-style error string. It also re-enables tool_bitcoin.py and interface_gui.py on Windows now that output/exit-code capture works, with interface_gui.py additionally gaining a vcpkg-Qt-specific skip.
result.problem: On Windows, anything invoking bitcoin.exe (test harnesses, CI, operator scripts) could not tell if the underlying bitcoind/bitcoin-node/bitcoin-gui child succeeded or failed, since the wrapper always reported exit code 0 and produced no captured output. This blocked functional test coverage of the wrapper and GUI startup on Windows and could mislead any script relying on the wrapper's exit status.

It also unblocks #36190 and re-enabled functional tests, giving it some leverage, but the blast radius is limited to Windows users of the wrapper.

result.card: This PR fixes a Windows-specific bug where bitcoin.exe's wrapper used _execvp and exited immediately after spawning bitcoind/bitcoin-node/bitcoin-gui, so any caller (scripts, CI, the test framework) could never see the child's real exit code or output; it switches to _spawnvp+_cwait, fixes an msvcrt EINVAL quirk in path lookup, corrects an errno-category bug that produced misleading Win32 error text, and re-enables two functional tests (tool_bitcoin.py, interface_gui.py) that were previously skipped on Windows because of this bug. The strongest evidence of importance is the description itself and the linked history (#33229, #35551) showing these tests were disabled specifically due to this defect, plus the shared commits with #36190 which depends on this fix landing. Review state is essentially ready: two members gave concept ACKs, prior review comments (attribution wording, AI-policy question, undocumented CRT behavior) were addressed across several force-pushes, and the only open items are a minor error-message inconsistency noted by cyb3ralbert and hebasto's suggestion that one commit may now be droppable following the merge of #33593. Impact is confined to Windows users and tooling around the bitcoin wrapper, so this is a solid but platform-scoped bug fix rather than a broad correctness or security issue.
